  Mayor’s Fund Subcommittee

  • Vice-chair Kimberly Lewis provided an update, the subcommittee is working
  on drafting a new SOP with updated language and they will be reviewing the
  MOU at the next subcommittee meeting.
  Policy Subcommittee
  • Chair Julie Lie provided an update, the subcommittee will continue their
  discussion on the 2025-2026 policy recommendations to the Mayor and City
  Council.
  • The subcommittee will be discussing youth homelessness at the next
  meeting on March 10, 2025.
  CoC Updates
  • Vice-chair Kimberly Lewis provided an update, the board and city staff
  discussed homeless challenges, safety concerns and challenges.
  • Bureau Manager Paul Duncan provided an update on the CoC General
  meetings, noting that they will be moved in coordination with the LB Coalition
  to help promote more advocacy.

  A motion was made by Voting Member Russell, seconded by Voting Member
  Scott, to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  6  Chotiswatdi, Russell, Scott, Wood, Lewis, Lie
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 4  Bedy, Hilliard, Howat, Killion

3.  25-54460  Recommendation to receive and file the Long Beach Tiny Home Shelter Program
  presentation by Paul Duncan from the Health Department.

  • Bureau Manager Paul Duncan gave an informational presentation on Tiny
  Homes Shelter program. On June 28th 2022 Long Beach was awarded a
  Project Homekey Round 2 grant for $5,616,752 to plan, purchase and
  program 33 modular, non-congregate, Tiny Home shelter units.
  • In August 2023 the MSC was deemed not feasible for residential use for at
  least 15 years due to upcoming Port construction projects.
  • A memo was released informing the community about the potential for
  locating the Tiny Home Project at E. Spring and California Ave. during the
  design and site exploration it was found that the soil compaction at the site
  would require significant work.. The site was no longer considered cost-
  effective.
  • City staff presented the Tiny Homes project to the LBCC Board of Trustees
  as a potential partnership opportunity. Due to difficulties with the approval
  process, the partnership would not be moving forward. The California

  Page 2 of 5
   HOMELESS SERVICES ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES
  WEDNESDAY, MARCH 5, 2025
  4811 AIRPORT PLAZA DR.
  PACIFIC GATEWAY, 4:30 PM

  Department of Housing and Community Development (HCD) informed staff
  that the Project Homekey funding must be returned in full to the state,
  amounting to $5,616,752.
  • A overview of the PHK Grant Funds was provided, $2,680,267 was allocated
  from the City General Fund to repay the state grant funds that had been
  expended.
  • City staff and committee members held discussions about potential
  alternatives for the Tiny Homes project. Committee members brainstormed
  various opportunities for the city team to explore.
  • A member of the public expressed concern about Long Beach being a large
  city with little progress on addressing homelessness. He suggested that the
  military and port should contribute by offering property to support efforts for
  housing the unhoused.
  • A member of the public suggested exploring local business initiatives or
  incentives to help support projects aimed at assisting the unhoused.

  A motion was made by Member Chotiswatdi, seconded by Voting Member
  Killion, to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following
  vote:

  Yes:  7  Chotiswatdi, Killion, Russell, Scott, Wood, Lewis, Lie
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 3  Bedy, Hilliard, Howat

4.  25-54499  Recommendation to receive and file the Homeless Services Bureau Staff
  Operations and Updates Report by Paul Duncan from the Health Department.

  • Bureau Manager Paul Duncan provided staffing updates.
  • Long Beachwas awarded $11.05M through the Encampment Resolution
  Fund (ERF) Round 3, the project will focus on the LA Riverbed providing
  additional outreach. The program will launch in the summer.
  • The state announced HHAP Round 6 Notice of Funding Availability, the
  application are due August 29, 2025.
  • Bitfocus phase 1 of the HMIS merger with LAHSA has been completed. Staff
  are starting the matching process for the units being created through the LA
  County PHK sites.
  • City staff are working with HUD technical assistance in order to ensure that
  current contracts are processed in a timely manner. HUD intends to reduce
  staffing and will be shutting down many offices.
  • Paul Duncan encouraged committee members to share their thoughts on the
  kinds of information they would like to see in future staff reports.

  • A member of the public voices concern on the PIT Count project and the

PUBLIC COMMENT

  • A member of the public has raised concerns about an encampment located near a facility that
  serves young adults on the autism spectrum. The individual expressed worry for their safety,
  reporting that two residents have been physically assaulted.

ANNOUNCEMENTS

  • Vice-Chair Lewis commented on the shelter projects A Bridge Home facility in Wilmington
  shutting down and expressed interest in whether Long Beach could take over its operations.
  This shelter was managed by U.S VETS.
